reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows that Ti- and Zn-containing intermetallics and a mixed MgO/ZnO/TiO₂ film contribute to passivation and corrosion resistance in MgTiZn alloys, but it does not demonstrate segregation-driven Ti rejection from Mg-rich intermetallics, nor that a predominantly TiO₂ layer forms from such segregation, nor that annealing improves properties over an as-cast baseline. The key mechanistic premises about segregation, Ti redistribution, and TiO₂-dominated passivation are therefore unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Mg-rich intermetallic formation can be driven by segregation during annealing
Ti is rejected from Mg-rich intermetallics and localizes at interfaces/grain boundaries
Ti-enriched regions preferentially form a stable TiO₂ passivation layer
A TiO₂-rich surface layer enhances corrosion and high-temperature oxidation resistance
Annealing-induced segregation improves corrosion/oxidation over as-cast homogeneous state
